about: The dimensions tools/parity.py checks (docs/PARITY.md). A check is one Go test whose expected values are Slack's own output: Slack's JavaScript run in node, or answers and messages captured from live Slack. Tests whose expected values someone wrote by hand from reading Slack's code are rules, and they don't go here. A check with a "snapshot" reads Slack's values from that file (its "slack" block says where they came from, and --refresh can capture them again); the others keep them in the test and say where they came from in "oracle". The areas list every part of Slack's client Clack implements, so the report can name the ones no check covers.

areas.name: Composer: the ":" emoji list
areas.gaps: Ranking only, for a few queries. Skin tones, the list's drawing and keyboard handling are not compared with Slack's output.

areas.name: Composer: the "@", "#" and "/" lists
areas.gaps: Only the fuzzy matcher's similarity is differential. The ranking of people, channels, usergroups and commands is tested against rules (TestAutocompleteSlackPeople, TestAutocompleteSlackChannels, TestAutocompleteSlackCommandsAndEmoji), not against Slack's output.

areas.name: Composer: formatting and markdown
areas.gaps: Only Mod+Shift+F (convertMarkdown) is differential. Markdown applied while typing and the formatting bar are tested against rules.

areas.name: Composer: link and message slugs
areas.gaps: The elements' shapes only. Slack's server computes a link slug's display_url, so Clack has nothing of its own to compare there; fakeslack's copy of it is checked as a fake-server check.

areas.name: Composer: sending, editing, drafts and scheduling
Messages: rich text, Block Kit, attachments and unfurls
Messages: the hover toolbar and the message menus
areas.gaps: Which buttons and rows show, their labels and groups, for a regular member of a Grid workspace (Karim's experiment groups) in a channel, the thread pane and the Threads view: plain, rich-text, bot (attachment), app (Block Kit), file, system, ephemeral, deleted and restricted messages; saved, completed and to-do ones; channels, private channels, DMs, group DMs, archived, unjoined and posting-restricted channels. Not compared: what an action does once chosen (its writes, modals and toasts), the keys on a focused message, the toolbar's width-dependent truncation (message_actions_truncate's presentation), a right-click on a message's content (links, images, files, mentions, reactions, its time), search results, Activity, Saved and the other containers, admins, owners, guests, channel managers and shared channels, canvas comment threads, Slack AI and Agentforce actions beyond one case (Slackbot AI's DM; the cases' workspace has no Slack AI), plugin rows (Slick's MAMenu), and submenus past their first level (Connect to apps' shortcuts, the reminder presets). The Threads view's Clack side is mirrored in the test (views imports messages), which fails when views/threads.go's right-click or its lack of a toolbar changes.

areas.name: Files and snippet previews
areas.gaps: Only the snippet HTML cut (html-truncate) is differential. The inline video player's rules (fileIsPlayableVideo, the pill's time, the mute and volume prefs) are read from Slack's code; no check compares them with Slack's output.

areas.name: Threads
areas.gaps: A link or pill without thread_ts into an AI app's DM opens the DM at the message; Slack's jumpViaRoutes (wc0P) opens it as a thread in the main window, or the app's chat tab, when AI apps are on and the app is valid (OePe K, Db4L wP, 3NYU yk). Clack doesn't model AI-app DMs yet.

areas.name: Home, DMs, Later and the other views
Invite people
areas.gaps: Splitting and tokenizing the typed addresses only. The modal's sends and answers are tested against rules.

areas.name: Themes and colours
areas.gaps: Only the custom-colour palettes (HCT) are differential.

areas.name: Desktop notifications
areas.gaps: The macOS options and the Windows text cut and ids. The Windows toast's layout differs from Slack's on purpose (see the deliberate differences).

areas.name: Desktop window placement
areas.gaps: Default and reopened bounds and the fit on a display only.

areas.name: Emoji rendering and the emoji picker

dimensions.what: Which hover toolbar buttons and which ⋮ and right-click menu rows a message gets, by its kind, its conversation and where it is shown.

checks.compares: Per case, the toolbar's buttons in order with their labels (the quick reactions and ⋮ included, or no toolbar), and the ⋮ and right-click menus' groups (or no right-click menu), each row's action id and label and its submenu's rows: actions_MessageActions, MessageActions and MessageActionButtonEllipsis; the ⋮ menu through renderMoreActionsMenu, MessageActionsOverflowMenu and MessageActionsMenu; the right-click menu through MessageActionsContextMenu (DtN2), its no-menu guard included, as the channel list and the thread pane render it. Clack's side: the toolbar's rules, the ⋮ menu the toolbar opens and the list's own right-click path (listState.contextMenu).

dimensions.what: The ":" list's ranking over the standard emoji set and custom emoji, in internal/acrank.

checks.compares: The ":" list's first 25 rows, in order, per query, model, frecency pref and emoji_v17 group (Slack's 16.0 and 17.0 sets).
The ":" list's rows, in order, and the first row's shown name and score, with synthetic custom emoji and aliases merged after the standard set.

oracle.source: the same Searcher path, custom emoji stored as dQ/Y upserts them and merged by Ak7A getConsolidatedEmoji

checks.compares: The order of keyword-only matches (score Inf) for :tu over five emoji, and :like matching +1 alone, with the fallback model.
checks.notes: The KeywordsMayMatch asserts in the same test are rules.

dimensions.what: The ":" list as the composer and popups.AutocompleteEmoji build it, end to end.

checks.compares: The ":" rows popups.AutocompleteEmoji gives (Clack's emoji index with custom emoji) for each query, in order.
checks.notes: The alias row's image and skin-tone asserts after the cases are rules.

checks.compares: The composer's ":tu" list end to end over the fake API: tulip first and root_vegetable second, no +1, the keyword matches present.
checks.notes: Only the first rows and which emoji appear come from Slack's output. The frecency steps later in the test are rules.

checks.compares: Tab on ":tu" takes the custom alias tu, and the composer's first five rows once the remote model is in.

With emoji_v17 off, on and off again (forced through core): ":tu"'s row 25 (fallback model) and the ":orc" rows (remote model) popups.AutocompleteEmoji gives, and the picker's groups against Slack's category tables (each group's size, the Objects runs the 17.0 table reorders).

oracle.source: the emoji-rank Searcher path, --exp=emoji_v17=on for the 17.0 set; getStandardEmojiCategories' tables 7Kvt and 6tVA (client-boot bbd3a8c1f7bb6f10)

checks.notes: The search, shrug, dancers' tones and image URL asserts in the same test are rules.

checks.compares: The composer's ":orc" rows end to end over the fake API, emoji_v17 off, on and off again, once the remote model is in.

oracle.source: the emoji-rank Searcher path, --exp=emoji_v17=on for the 17.0 set

checks.compares: PositionAwareFuzzyMatcher's similarity for query and name pairs, to 1e-8.

dimensions.what: Mod+Shift+F: typed markdown converted to formatting.

Mod+Shift+F on documents that already hold formats, mentions, emoji or block formats.

checks.notes: The round trip and delta asserts in the same test are rules.

checks.compares: Moving the window to the primary screen: the fit and the centring, JavaScript's rounding included.

dimensions.what: Desktop notifications: the macOS options, the Windows text cut and notification ids.

checks.compares: The options Slack's mac shell hands Electron's Notification for each sample payload (internal/ui/testdata/usernotify_slack.json).

oracle.source: ld, h6 and class h0, run with Electron's Notification stubbed

checks.compares: The Windows shell's cut of toast text: words, the cap, UTF-16 units, a cut through a surrogate pair.
buildNotificationId, its digest past 64 characters included, and parseNotificationId reading it back.

dimensions.what: fakeslack's link slug display_url, which tests that paste links run against.

checks.compares: fakeslack's display_url for each URL against the live chat.slugifyUrl answer for it.
checks.notes: Clack shows the server's display_url. This checks the fake server other tests run against, not Clack.

dimensions.what: The thread pane's history: how each replies read's page goes into the thread's slices, and which slice the pane draws from its start.

checks.compares: The slices and reachedStart, reachedEnd and prevReachedEnd after each page, live reply, deletion, disconnect and truncation, and the slice getPotentiallyOutdatedTimestamps picks at a dozen starts, for six page sequences.

oracle.source: client-boot 6Yed (addTimestamps, removeTimestamp, resetReachedEnd, truncateChannelHistory) over om2Z, and dTxY's getTimestampsByChannelId and getPotentiallyOutdatedTimestamps

dimensions.what: The parts of Quip's edit protocol Clack writes and reads for canvases (internal/quip): protobuf bytes, order keys, RTML text, parsing and writing.

checks.compares: The bytes of requests, save bundles (edited, new, deleted and checked sections, list items, the five control kinds, the title with its rich text) and answers, against p8gD.toBinary's: field order, set zeros and empty messages, packed numbers, negative int32s.
Slack's bytes for the same messages read back to the same fields and written again to the same bytes.

oracle.source: p8gD.toBinary over QkBk and o3+F (the quip-wire-encode snapshot)

checks.compares: What Slack's decoder keeps of bytes a server could send (fields out of order, repeated, packed or not, unknown fields and groups, Slack's fields Clack doesn't name, malformed input), written back: p8gD.fromBinary then toBinary. Refusals compare as refusals, not by message.
0fa5.generate's key between two others, carries, temp suffixes and bad input included.
W77Y.escapeText and isSafeUri.

fce5.getTextAndMarks: the text and every mark (name, value, UTF-16 offsets) of RTML through the HTML parser and W77Y's walker: entities, line breaks, controls, links, annotations, formatting with attributes, misnesting, dropped and unwrapped tags, nested tags that make Slack give up.
The editor's getCompactRtml on text and marks (overlaps, density order, ties, empty marks, link attributes), and Slack's own parse-then-write round trip of every parse case.

A save's bundle section for each edit Clack makes (typed text, a ticked or unticked box, a deleted section) of every kind of section (paragraphs, headings, list items under each list style, code with its language, the title), byte for byte against Slack's own section entity: ZRIn.toUpdateBundle over EKJU.toPb with the setters' dirty fields, then WJQ2.shouldAddToActivityStack against the server's copy.

The title metadata every save sends (extractTitleMetadata(true)): the title text (the export's text, trimmed, cut at 255 UTF-16 units, Untitled when empty) and its rich text (30B3.convertSectionsToRichTextApiPb), from titles with entities, spaces, formatting and long text. A title Clack refuses (a link) is a known divergence.

A text section's RTML after an edit (ApplyRuns: the editor's runs over the base, controls kept where their runs are, comment anchors and a link's attributes carried with their characters, typed spaces kept as the pre-wrap editor holds them, a section with an empty mark refused), against Slack's save writer: CITi's DI over the DOM the RTML builds gives the same bytes back.

A new section's bundle section, byte for byte, as Slack's editor saves one it made after another (paragraphs, headings, list items of each style at their level, a ticked checklist item, an empty one, formatted text): K2FO.createNewSection's fresh entity, setSectionAttribute and initSibling, then toUpdateBundle and the activity row.

deliberate.slack: Slack desktop's toastXml (EH.createToastNotification, 4.53.276 win32) has a header, a reply box and line limits, and titles a message toast with the channel's name.
deliberate.clack: Clack's toast is Chrome's (Chromium's notification_template_builder.cc): the title as the webapp wrote it ("New message in #general"), the body, the workspace, Clack's icon, the time.

deliberate.what: A slack://channel link whose thread_ts names a reply
deliberate.slack: handleParsedDeepLink (boot-render VxbD) sends slack://channel?id=C&thread_ts=<reply> to jumpToMessage, which opens toThread keyed on the reply; ThreadView (eTbq) takes the reply as rootMsg (getMessage(ch, threadTs)) and requestReplies (client-boot 0VEE) keeps what conversations.replies answers for that ts, the whole thread parent first. So Slack (build 2c0d02ca130f) draws a broken pane: the reply as the root, the parent and its siblings under it.
deliberate.clack: A logged guard opens the reply's thread at the reply instead, its root highlighted in the conversation: jumpViaRoutes for a reply core holds (ui: jumpToMessage: its thread_ts … is a reply in …), OpenThread's guard for a route naming one (ui: thread open: …), the pane's hand-over once conversations.replies says so (ui: thread pane: its root … is a reply in …). It never stands in for fixing a caller that builds a reply-rooted route: Clack's own routes take the reply's thread first, as Slack's do.
deliberate.decided: thread-open-root's parity review, 2026-11-18 (kept as a logged guard, recorded here with this evidence)

elsewhere.what: TestIconsMatchSlack and TestArtMatchesSlack: Clack's icons and illustrations against the glyphs of Slack's icon font and its SVG art, by ink, with pass/fail thresholds.
TestTextMatchesChrome and TestTextInk: Clack's text against Chrome's in the same font, with thresholds, plus text_render_compare.py's side-by-sides.
sidebar_rows_ref.py and rail_ref.py: the sidebar's rows and the rail next to Slack's markup under Slack's shipping CSS, measured. Pass/fail only with SIDEBAR_ROWS_STRICT.
compact_ref.py: channel and thread rows, Clean and Compact, next to Slack's markup under Slack's CSS; it fails when a row height is off by more than 1px.
activity_ref.py: Activity rows next to Slack's markup under Slack's CSS. Side-by-sides, no pass/fail.
threads_ref.py: the thread pane's states in Slack's markup under Slack's CSS. Side-by-sides, no pass/fail.
emoji_render_compare.py: Clack's standard emoji against Chrome's, cell by cell. No pass/fail.
